summary: Frontend-only verification of the 10-digit mobile-number restriction on the Login page. All 8 UI/integration checks passed: maxLength=10 attribute present, input clamps at 10 digits when typed or JS-pasted, non-digits stripped, short-number (5-digit) submission is blocked client-side with toast 'Enter a 10-digit mobile number' and ZERO /auth/request-otp calls fired, exactly-10 super-admin phone triggers 200 request-otp with mock OTP toast and advances to OTP step, super-admin end-to-end OTP verify redirects to /super-admin, tenant login at /t/demo enforces same maxLength=10 clamp and Send OTP succeeds, reviewer 9898989898 send-otp still works, and wrong OTP shows readable 'Invalid OTP' toast (no '[object Object]').
critical_code_review_comments: Login.jsx is 367 lines and mixes phone/OTP UI, demo-login panel, and tenant role tabs. Consider splitting demo-login block and hero panel into subcomponents for readability.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Login.jsx phone input has maxLength={10} attribute (line 234) and onChange slicing to 10 digits (line 236); sendOtp() rejects phone.length !== 10 with toast before API. All flows verified against public URL. Tenant login path is /t/:slug (not /t/:slug/login).
rca of the issue: n/a — this iteration was verification of a UI restriction that main agent had already implemented. No bug found.
